summary: Corrected 243 passages or structure issues. Rule 1: 198, Rule 2: 55, Rule 3: 1, Rule 4: 15, Rule 5: 1, Rule 6: 178, Rule 7: 21, Rule 8: 86.
counting_note: A passage may violate more than one rule. Counts by rule overlap.

findings.original: Agree with Ben: put the packed address mapping inside a typed view, and keep storage ownership separate. Introduce this first for the existing value cache and row-major key cache. Then place PR #4424 on top, with packed-key addressing inside the new type and attention algorithms outside it.
findings.fix: Use a view that calculates where each value is stored in memory. Keep the object that owns that memory separate. Introduce this interface for the existing key and value caches before changing the key layout in pull request #4424.

findings.original: It asks for one worker-aware save_k interface.
findings.fix: It asks for a save_k function that each participating thread can call.

findings.original: Ben questions a separate layout type. He does not equate ownership, mapping, and views. His sketch remains a starting point.
findings.fix: Ben questions whether a separate layout type is needed. His example still separates the object that stores the values from the object that accesses them.

findings.original: Another agent should implement the parent change from this handoff.
findings.fix: Another agent should implement the first pull request from this design.

findings.original: Scope clarification: physical addressing and row movement can become local to the tensor implementation. Query packing, matrix multiplication, dispatch, and worker coordination still change outside it in PR #4424. This qualifies the proposed split; it does not reject Ben’s suggestion.
findings.fix: The tensor implementation can contain the address calculations and row-copy operations. PR #4424 still needs changes to query layout, matrix multiplication, kernel selection, and thread coordination. Those changes remain outside the tensor implementation.

findings.original: Source and time, UTC
findings.fix: Source and time in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)

findings.original: Extend save_k with a worker index and call it from both the main thread and helpers.
findings.fix: Add a thread index to save_k , the function that stores key rows. Call it from the main thread and its helper threads.

findings.original: Use the existing tensor , dtensor , and expr precedent.
findings.fix: Follow the interfaces already used by tensor , dtensor , and expr .

findings.original: Accept. A wrapper with only at() and unrelated free functions would not fully meet this request.
findings.fix: Accept. An at() method for reading one element is not enough. The new type must also support the existing expression interface.

findings.original: #3: Claude sketch and reservation
findings.fix: #3: Claude’s example and Ben’s concern

findings.original: Sketches separate mapping, ownership, and borrowed access. Ben questions the need for a separate k_vnni_layout type.
findings.fix: Shows separate types for the address calculation, storage, and access to that storage. Ben questions the need for k_vnni_layout , a type used only for address calculation.

findings.original: Combine mapping and borrowed access in concrete view types. Retain inline owned storage and optimized operations.
findings.fix: Put each address calculation in the corresponding view type. Keep the value array inside the storage object. Preserve the optimized operations.

findings.original: The full fetched text is saved in the review evidence .
findings.fix: The saved review file contains the full comment text. [Review evidence]

findings.original: Keep from Claude: inline aligned storage, restricted raw access, explicit constness, optimized row/block operations, typed kernel parameters, and safe owner-to-view lifetimes.
findings.fix: Keep from Claude: store the array inside its owner, at the alignment required by the vector instructions. Limit direct pointer access to implementation code. Make read-only access explicit. Preserve optimized row and block operations. Use parameter types that identify each kernel’s expected layout. Prevent views from outliving their storage.

findings.original: Simplify: a concrete view owns its coordinate-to-address function. There is no public Layout template parameter or separately instantiated layout object.
findings.fix: Simplify: each view type contains its address calculation. It needs no public Layout template parameter. It needs no separate layout object.

findings.original: Add from Ben’s earlier request: real expr integration, row expressions, conversion, and bounded logical slicing.
findings.fix: Add from Ben’s earlier request: support the existing expr interface. Allow row expressions, value conversion, and access to selected rows and dimensions with bounds checks.

findings.original: Follow repository const behavior: const matrix indexing produces read-only rows. Claude’s span-like sketch permits writing through a const mutable handle. These differ. Use the repository convention here.
findings.fix: Follow the repository’s read-only behavior: indexing a const matrix view returns a read-only row. Claude’s example permits writes through a view even when the view object is const . Use the repository behavior here.

findings.original: Storage owner Contains inline bytes. Controls object lifetime.
findings.fix: Storage owner Contains the value array. Controls how long the storage exists.

findings.original: Concrete view Borrows bytes. Contains shape + mapping.
findings.fix: View Accesses the owner’s storage. Calculates each value’s address.

findings.original: Logical row / kernel Uses expressions or a typed kernel argument.
findings.fix: Row operation or kernel Uses the view to read or write values.

findings.original: The arrow means “provides access,” not “allocates.” A view does not own the memory. No separate public layout layer is needed.
findings.fix: Each arrow means “provides access.” The view uses storage owned by another object. Its type includes the address calculation.

findings.original: 3. Build the abstraction on main first
findings.fix: 3. Add the tensor interface to main first

findings.original: New row-expression contract.
findings.fix: Rows support the expression interface.

findings.original: Shared K save.
findings.fix: Threads share the K-store work.

findings.original: The abstraction has value before K packing. The parent needs no new AMX feature or shared-save machinery.
findings.fix: The interface improves access to the existing cache layouts. The first pull request needs no new AMX feature. It does not change how threads divide the K-store work.

findings.original: Live PR base reported by GitHub. Its object is present locally. Start the parent from main, refreshing and reviewing changes if main has advanced.
findings.fix: GitHub reported this as the pull request’s base commit during the design review. This commit exists locally. Start the first pull request from main. Fetch and review newer main changes before implementation.

findings.fix: GitHub and the local checkout used this same commit during the design review.

findings.original: At the reviewed main revision, K is row-major and V is already pair-interleaved in the 16-lane build. The cache header is unchanged between the common ancestor and reviewed main. This is direct evidence that the abstraction can precede PR #4424.
findings.fix: At the reviewed main revision, K uses row-major storage. V already uses paired-token storage in the build with 16 fp32 values per vector instruction. The cache header is unchanged between the common ancestor and reviewed main. The tensor interface can therefore be added before PR #4424.

findings.original: Do not copy whole current-branch files into the parent. Main has independent model and CI changes after the common ancestor.
findings.fix: Do not copy whole files from the PR #4424 branch into the first pull request. Main contains separate model and CI changes made after the branches diverged.

findings.original: Do not interpret a direct main-to-child diff as the child patch. It also shows main changes absent from the older branch.
findings.fix: A direct comparison of main with PR #4424 includes more than that pull request’s changes. It also includes main changes absent from the older branch.

findings.original: Keep the parent free of TRON_K_VNNI , packed-K kernels, helper state, and generated worker calls.
findings.fix: Exclude TRON_K_VNNI , the build option that enables packed K, from the first pull request. Also exclude packed-K kernels, helper-thread state, and generated calls to helper threads.

findings.original: 4. Keep logical coordinates stable
findings.fix: 4. Keep token and dimension indexing unchanged

findings.original: A small physical-order example
findings.fix: Example: the order of values in memory

findings.original: Only physical order changes. A logical row still means one token’s dimensions.
findings.fix: Only the order in memory changes. A row still contains one token’s dimensions.

findings.original: bf16 element offset, not bytes
findings.fix: Position from the start of the plane, in bf16 elements

findings.original: Native K; AVX2 V
findings.fix: Native K and AVX2 V

findings.original: Parent and unchanged fallback.
findings.fix: First pull request. Keep the existing row-major path.

findings.original: Parent, for the existing 16-lane V configuration.
findings.fix: First pull request, for V in the build with 16 fp32 values per vector instruction.

findings.original: Child only. Retain its existing gate and 64-token × 128-dimension kernel restriction.
findings.fix: PR #4424 only. Keep the existing layout-selection condition. Keep the kernel restricted to 64 tokens × 128 dimensions.

findings.original: The packed-K formula divides dimensions into groups of 32 and tokens into groups of 16. A transpose of the V view alone does not produce this blocked order.
findings.fix: The packed-K formula uses groups of 32 dimensions and groups of 16 tokens. Exchanging V’s row and column coordinates alone does not produce this order.

findings.original: The new V owner initially supports positive even row counts and positive column counts divisible by the selected SIMD chunk width. Production cache use must retain the existing stricter store and reduction restrictions. Do not claim that representing a matrix makes every attention kernel support it.
findings.fix: The new V storage type requires a positive even number of rows. Its column count must be positive and divisible by the number of values in one SIMD chunk. Keep the existing, stricter shape restrictions for cache stores and weighted sums. A tensor type can represent a shape that an attention kernel does not support.

findings.original: 8,192 bf16 elements; 7 anchor coordinates
findings.fix: 8,192 bf16 elements and 7 selected coordinates with known positions

findings.original: Every coordinate maps to its independently enumerated physical position. These are arithmetic checks of the design, not tests of a C++ implementation.
findings.fix: The script lists values in storage order and checks every calculated position against that list. All positions match. This checks the formulas in the design. It does not test a C++ implementation.

findings.original: Tron; main; PR Tron is this repository’s inference system. main is its integration branch. PR means pull request.
findings.fix: Tron, main, pull request Tron is this repository’s inference system. main is the integration branch. A pull request (PR) proposes code changes for review.

findings.original: Q, K, V; KV cache A token’s query, key, and value vectors. The cache stores earlier keys and values for attention.
findings.fix: Q, K, V, KV cache Q, K, and V are a token’s query, key, and value vectors. The KV cache stores earlier keys and values for attention.

findings.original: Rank-2 tensor; row-major A matrix indexed by two coordinates. Row-major storage places each row’s dimensions consecutively.
findings.fix: Tensor, rank, row-major A tensor holds values indexed by coordinates. Rank is the number of coordinates needed to select a value. A rank-2 tensor is a matrix. Row-major storage places the values of each row consecutively in memory.

findings.original: VNNI; packed V; blocked packed K Vector Neural Network Instructions. Packed V pairs tokens within each dimension. PR #4424’s packed K pairs dimensions within blocks of tokens. These are distinct layouts.
findings.fix: VNNI, native K, packed V, blocked packed K VNNI means Vector Neural Network Instructions. Here, “packed” means the values are ordered for vector or matrix instructions. Native K stores one token’s dimensions consecutively. Packed V alternates values from two adjacent tokens within each dimension. PR #4424’s blocked packed K groups dimension pairs within token blocks. These are different layouts.

findings.original: bf16; fp16; fp32; NaN Brain floating-point with 16 bits; IEEE half with 16 bits; IEEE single with 32 bits; a “not a number” floating-point value.
findings.fix: bf16, fp16, fp32, NaN bf16 is the 16-bit brain floating-point format. fp16 is the standard 16-bit half-precision format. fp32 is the standard 32-bit single-precision format. NaN is a floating-point “not a number” value.

findings.original: SIMD; AVX2; AVX-512; chunk Instructions operating on several values at once. The selected vector instruction family is AVX2 or AVX-512. A chunk is the implementation’s group of 8 or 16 fp32 lanes.
findings.fix: SIMD, AVX2, AVX-512, chunk, lane SIMD means single instruction, multiple data values. AVX2 and AVX-512 are processor instruction families for vector operations. A chunk contains 8 or 16 fp32 values in the selected build. A lane is one value’s position in a vector.

findings.original: AMX; QK; PV Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions. QK computes query–key scores. PV combines attention weights with values.
findings.fix: AMX, QK, PV AMX means Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions. QK computes query–key scores. PV combines attention weights with values.

findings.original: expr; tensor; dtensor The expression interface, host tensor owner, and hardware-oriented tensor type already in Tron.
findings.fix: expr, tensor, dtensor expr is Tron’s common interface for reading computed or stored values. tensor stores values in host memory. dtensor stores values in a form used by hardware operations.

findings.original: Page; slot; geometry; plane A page holds 64 token positions. A slot is a persistent cache region for one layer or several sharing layers. Geometry specifies head count and width. A plane holds either K or V for one head in one page.
findings.fix: Page, slot, geometry, plane, attention head A page holds 64 token positions. A slot is a cache region used by one layer or shared by several layers. An attention head uses one set of query, key, and value vectors. Geometry specifies the head count and the dimension count per head. A plane holds K or V for one head in one page.

findings.original: book; arena; EAGLE book owns cache pages and backing allocations. An arena is one backing memory region. EAGLE is the speculative model with an additional cache storage region.
findings.fix: book, arena, EAGLE book owns cache pages and their memory allocations. An arena is one allocated memory region. EAGLE is the speculative model with an additional cache storage region.

findings.original: DMA; FPGA; GOF Direct memory access; field-programmable gate array; the grouped attention work and staging object named gof in the code.
findings.fix: DMA, FPGA, GOF DMA means direct memory access. FPGA means field-programmable gate array. GOF names the gof object that groups attention work and prepares data for transfer.

findings.original: CI; Slice; Nix; fake Continuous integration; the repository test scheduler; its pinned build environment; tests using simulated hardware through pos_fake .
findings.fix: CI, Slice, Nix, fake CI means continuous integration: automated builds and tests. Slice is the repository’s test scheduler. Nix supplies the build environment with fixed tool versions. A fake-hardware test uses simulated hardware through the pos_fake library.

findings.original: Storage owner
findings.fix: The owner contains the values and controls how long they remain valid. A view accesses those values without owning their storage.

findings.original: Contains shape + mapping.
findings.fix: The layout is the order of values in memory. The mapping calculates a value’s address from its coordinates.

findings.original: bounded logical slicing.
findings.fix: A logical row contains one token’s dimensions, regardless of storage order. A slice selects rows or dimensions without copying their values.

findings.original: dispatch
findings.fix: A kernel performs a specific computation. Dispatch selects which kernel to call.

findings.original: parent
findings.fix: The first pull request introduces this interface on main. PR #4424 will depend on it. The diagrams call these the parent and child.

findings.original: Live PR base reported by GitHub.
findings.fix: A commit records one version of the code. A pull request’s base is the version it changes. Its head is its latest commit. The common ancestor is the latest commit shared by both branches.

findings.original: The domain-only glossary is also saved in CONTEXT.md . Function names in the rest of this report are defined at their first substantive use.
findings.fix: The cache terms are also defined in the project glossary. [CONTEXT.md]

findings.original: Short version
findings.fix: Keep only the three-sentence summary here. Move the detailed findings to “What Ben asked for”.

findings.original: 2. Words used here
findings.fix: Move “Words used here” before the review so its definitions precede their use.

findings.original: The declarations below are an interface sketch. They are not compiled code. Keep definitions in namespace tron and follow existing attributes and formatting.
findings.fix: The declarations below describe the proposed interfaces. They have not been compiled. Keep their definitions in namespace tron, the C++ name group for Tron types. Keep the existing C++ attributes (annotations attached to declarations). Follow the existing formatting.

findings.original: vnni_tensor owns one inline aligned array of bf16 values. Its name describes the standard pair-interleaved representation used by V. It performs no heap allocation.
findings.fix: vnni_tensor contains one array of bf16 values inside the tensor object. The array starts at the required memory alignment (an address divisible by the required byte count). Its name describes the standard representation that places pairs of V values together. It allocates no memory separately from the object.

findings.original: vnni_view<T, R, D> borrows that storage. Restrict T to bf16 or const bf16. Its private mapping implements the V formula above.
findings.fix: vnni_view<T, R, D> refers to that array without owning it. Restrict its element type T to bf16 or const bf16. The const form allows reads only. The view calculates element addresses internally with the V formula above.

findings.original: vnni_row<T, D> holds the pair base and token parity by value. It exposes the logical row. It must not pretend that its dimensions are contiguous.
findings.fix: vnni_row<T, D> stores the address of the first value in the token pair. It also stores whether its token is the even or odd member. It provides access to one token’s dimensions in logical order. It must not represent those dimensions as consecutive values in memory.

findings.original: The view derives directly from expr<view_type, R, D>. The row derives from expr<row_type, D>. The owner also forwards the rank-2 expression protocol through its view.
findings.fix: The view inherits the matrix expression interface expr<view_type, R, D> directly. The row inherits the vector expression interface expr<row_type, D>. The owner implements the matrix expression operations by calling its view.

findings.original: Provide dim, element, const_element, shape0(), and valid() consistently with existing views. Use dma = false: borrowing DMA-allocated bytes does not make a packed logical row suitable for direct row DMA.
findings.fix: Match the existing view definitions. dim describes the dimensions. element names the element type. const_element names its read-only form. Provide shape0() to return the first dimension’s size. Provide valid() to report whether the view refers to storage. Set dma = false to mark the logical row as unsuitable for direct row DMA. Allocation in DMA memory does not make the row’s values consecutive.

findings.original: The existing expression concept recognizes rank-1 expressions only. The matrix participates through the rank-2 expr base. Do not broaden that concept or derive from views<>, whose documented leaf contract requires contiguous rows. [S2]
findings.fix: The existing expression concept (a C++ rule that limits accepted types) recognizes expressions for one-dimensional vectors only. Keep the concept’s existing type restriction. The matrix uses the matrix form of the expr interface. Do not inherit from views<>, the interface whose final rows must contain consecutive values in memory. [S2]

findings.original: Required contract
findings.fix: Required behavior

findings.original: Logical bf16 scalar access with bounds assertions. Mutable access may update that scalar only. Const matrix indexing returns a read-only row.
findings.fix: Access one bf16 value by its logical coordinates. Assert that the coordinates are in range. Writable access may update only that value. Indexing a const matrix returns a read-only row.

findings.original: Read a logical fp32 chunk. Implement packed extraction using vector operations.
findings.fix: Read a chunk of fp32 values in logical order. Extract the packed values with vector operations (instructions that process several values together).

findings.original: Write the logical row and preserve its partner. Match existing expression conversion rules. Identical source/destination is supported.
findings.fix: Write the logical row. Preserve the other row in its stored pair. Match the existing expression conversion rules. Allow the source and destination to be the same row.

findings.original: Initialize complete pairs without reading old destination bytes, including on fresh storage. Evaluate both source chunks before each combined store. Support identical source/destination. Do not promise arbitrary overlapping shifted-source assignment.
findings.fix: Initialize complete pairs without reading old destination bytes. This must also work on storage that has not been initialized. Read or calculate both source chunks before storing their combined pair. Allow the source and destination to be the same matrix. Other overlapping copies need not work when the source and destination start at different positions.

findings.original: Rebind the handle. Use .set() for copying values, as existing views do.
findings.fix: Change which storage the view refers to. Use .set() to copy values, as existing views do.

findings.original: Mutable on a mutable lvalue owner; read-only on a const lvalue owner. Delete rvalue overloads. Apply the same restriction to owner indexing and every accessor returning borrowed data. Compute the view on demand.
findings.fix: Return a writable view from a writable owner used as an lvalue (an expression that names an existing object). Return a read-only view from a const lvalue owner. Delete overloads for rvalue owners (temporary values or objects marked for moving). An overload is an alternative with the same function name and different accepted arguments. Deleting it rejects matching calls at compile time. Apply the same restriction to owner indexing. Apply it to every function returning access to the owner’s storage without a copy. Create the view when requested.

findings.original: Copy inline data. Do not store a view pointing back into the owner. Preserve trivial copyability and trivial destruction.
findings.fix: Copy the array stored inside the object. Do not keep a view that points to the owner’s own array. Preserve trivial copyability (the C++ property that permits copying an object’s bytes to an object of the same type). Preserve trivial destruction (no custom cleanup when the object is destroyed).

findings.original: Accept a compatible rank-2 expression and initialize complete pairs through the matrix operation. Keep same-type copy/move special members defaulted. Retain an explicitly defaulted trivial default constructor.
findings.fix: Accept a compatible matrix expression. Initialize complete pairs through the matrix operation. Keep same-type copy and move operations defaulted (generated by the compiler with = default). Keep an explicitly defaulted default constructor, the function that creates an object without supplied values. It must remain trivial, with no custom initialization.

findings.original: Allow mutable-to-read-only views. Reject read-only-to-mutable conversion and mutation through read-only rows or slices.
findings.fix: Allow converting writable views to read-only views. Reject conversion in the other direction. Reject writes through read-only rows or slices (selected rows or dimensions of a tensor).

findings.original: Existing tensor construction and dtensor conversion can consume rank-2 expressions by reading their logical rows. Existing dotter, the native K dot-product helper, requires specific contiguous views. Keep native K on those existing types. [S3] [S4]
findings.fix: Existing tensor construction and dtensor conversion accept matrix expressions by reading their logical rows. Existing dotter, the helper that multiplies corresponding query and native K values and sums the products, requires specific views of consecutive values in memory. Keep native K on those existing types. [S3] [S4]

findings.original: Slicing without false contiguity
findings.fix: Select rows and dimensions without assuming consecutive storage

findings.original: Add narrow slice<Rows, Cols> overloads for the new matrix view and slice<Cols> for its row. Keep the existing call syntax.
findings.fix: Add slice<Rows, Cols> overloads that accept the new matrix view. Add slice<Cols> overloads that accept its row. Keep the existing form of the function calls.

findings.original: A slice retains the original plane stride plus logical row/column origins. Never recalculate packing from the sliced dimensions. A slice beginning at an odd token must retain that parity.
findings.fix: A slice retains the original plane stride (the spacing between stored row pairs). It also keeps the logical starting row and column. Never recalculate packing from the slice’s smaller dimensions. If a slice starts at an odd token, keep that token in the odd position of its stored pair.

findings.original: For implementation simplicity, initially require dimension slice origins and lengths to be whole SIMD chunks. Row origins may be odd. Reject unsupported slices explicitly.
findings.fix: Initially require a dimension slice to start at a whole SIMD chunk. Its length must also be a whole number of chunks. This limits implementation complexity. The starting row may be odd. Reject unsupported slices explicitly.

findings.original: Use a small internal slice expression holding the view and offsets by value. It must preserve writability and row bf16_chunk(). Do not extend the generic views<> hierarchy.
findings.fix: Use a small internal slice expression that stores its own copy of the view. Store the row and column offsets inside that expression. Keep writable slices writable. Keep the row’s bf16_chunk() operation available. Do not add types to the general views<> inheritance structure.

findings.original: Const matrix views produce read-only slices. Preserve that distinction before copying the handle into a slice. Reject slicing an rvalue owner through a concrete deleted overload or constraint. Deleting only as_view() && is insufficient: the existing generic expression slice accepts a const reference.
findings.fix: Const matrix views produce read-only slices. Preserve that read-only status before copying the view into a slice. Reject slicing an rvalue owner with an overload marked as deleted or a type restriction. Deleting only as_view() && is insufficient. The existing general expression slice accepts a const reference (read-only access that can also refer to a temporary object).

findings.original: Nested packed slices must also use value-owning handles and offsets. For the initial change, explicitly reject nested slicing unless these narrow overloads cover it. Never fall back to the existing reference-capturing generic expression slice for a temporary packed handle.
findings.fix: A slice of a packed slice must also store its own view and offsets. Initially reject these nested slices unless the new overloads support them. Never pass a temporary packed view to the existing general expression slice. That slice keeps a reference to its input object instead of copying it.

findings.original: Iteration may expose logical rows and elements. Iterators must carry pointer and coordinates by value. They must not borrow a temporary row object or claim to be contiguous iterators.
findings.fix: Iteration may visit rows and elements in logical order. Each iterator (an object that tracks a position during iteration) must store the array’s memory address and the coordinates directly. It must not depend on a temporary row object. It must not claim that successive logical values are consecutive in memory.

findings.original: This is a deliberate initial scope limit: arbitrary column tails, dynamic shapes, general transposes, and a universal layout-policy framework are excluded. Add no iterator framework unless needed for the logical operations above. [Existing slice and view contracts]
findings.fix: The initial implementation excludes: Dimension slices that end in a partial SIMD chunk. Shapes chosen at runtime. General transposes (operations that exchange rows and columns). A general system for selecting layouts through a policy type. Add no general iterator implementation unless the logical operations above require it. [Existing slice and view requirements]

findings.original: Separate cache append from ordinary assignment
findings.fix: Separate adding cache rows from ordinary assignment

findings.original: Keep a narrow internal operation named append_v_row for the cache write contract. It accepts a typed destination, token index, and a dimension-sized contiguous source view. Overload it for packed V and row-major V. Source types are bf16, fp16, and float.
findings.fix: Keep an internal operation named append_v_row to write a newly added cache row. It accepts a destination view whose type identifies the storage layout. It also accepts a token index and a source view containing one token’s consecutive dimension values. Provide overloads for packed V and row-major V. The accepted source types are bf16, fp16, and float.

findings.original: set_pair deliberately writes both rows. Evaluate both source chunks before storing their pair. Provide a fused zero-odd form for an even-token append. It must keep the current one-pass store without reading destination bytes.
findings.fix: set_pair writes both rows in a pair. Read or calculate both source chunks before storing the pair. Provide a form that adds an even token and zeros the odd row in the same pass. It must preserve the current store operation without reading destination bytes.

findings.original: An odd-token append preserves the even partner. Both append forms keep the existing source-type-specific conversion instructions.
findings.fix: Adding an odd token preserves the even row in its pair. Both forms keep the conversion instructions currently used for each source type.

findings.original: Place append_v_row in the internal tensor operation implementation. It performs no token allocation or completion notification. The cache chooses when append semantics apply.
findings.fix: Place append_v_row in the internal tensor operation implementation. It does not allocate tokens. It does not notify other work that the write is complete. The cache chooses when to use the behavior for a newly added row.

findings.original: Keep generic expression assignment separate from the packed-cache conversion policy. Do not route the packed fp16/float append overloads through generic bf16 expression conversion. The AVX2 row-major V overload must retain its existing row-view .set() conversion and write only the requested row.
findings.fix: Keep general expression assignment separate from the conversion rules for adding packed cache rows. Do not use general bf16 expression conversion in the packed fp16/float append overloads. The AVX2 row-major V overload must retain its existing row-view .set() conversion. It must write only the requested row.

findings.original: Typed page and kernel boundaries
findings.fix: Page and kernel arguments that identify the layout A kernel is a low-level calculation routine.

findings.original: Add page::k_tensor<geometry>(slot, head) and page::v_tensor<geometry>(slot, head) as borrowed matrix accessors. Native K returns its existing row-major view. V returns the compile-time selected packed or row-major view. Keep existing logical page convenience methods as thin adapters where needed.
findings.fix: Add page::k_tensor<geometry>(slot, head) to provide a matrix view of K without copying its values. Native K returns its existing row-major view. Add page::v_tensor<geometry>(slot, head) for V. V returns the packed or row-major view selected at compile time. Keep existing page methods where needed. Make them call the new logical operations.

findings.original: Preserve the existing remaining parameter order and names in the implementation. The sketch uses explanatory names. Ordinary model code passes views. Only the implementation of a layout-specific kernel obtains the physical address through an internal friend accessor.
findings.fix: Preserve the order and names of the remaining parameters in the implementation. The declarations above use explanatory names. Ordinary model code passes views. Only a kernel implementation for a specific layout obtains the storage address. It uses an internal friend accessor (a function permitted to read the view’s private members).

findings.original: No public packed .data, implicit pointer conversion, or public pointer constructor. Raw addresses must not silently acquire a packed type.
findings.fix: Do not expose a public .data member for packed storage. Do not allow automatic conversion to a pointer (a memory address). Do not expose a public constructor that creates a packed view from a pointer. A raw address must not automatically become a value of a packed type.

findings.original: Keep low-level access in detail::vnni_access. This is a code-organization boundary, not a security boundary.
findings.fix: Keep direct storage access in the internal helper detail::vnni_access. This groups that access in one part of the code. It does not enforce security restrictions.

findings.original: Make new storage trivially default-constructible, trivially copyable, and trivially destructible. Keep its default construction uninitialized. These C++ properties allow construction without setting values, bytewise copying, and destruction without cleanup. Leave the stored values uninitialized during default construction.
